data.title: The Human Condition of AI Content
data.subtitle: We asked people who work in commerce, content and AI one question. Should companies use AI to create content, and why? They answered in person at eTail Boston, by LinkedIn message and in a LinkedIn poll, in their own words.
bullets: 53% said yes, with a human owning the output. That is more than twice any other position, and in open answers people wrote it in themselves.
The people who said no get full space. Writers returned the highest no share of any group, and each person who said no gave a reason.
The most divided group builds AI for a living. AI practitioners spread across five positions, and 11% said it is not a choice to make.
US marketers did not give a single no. Results are reported by group, so you can see who said what.
What LinkedIn did before the study opened. A report button for AI slop, and a proofreading tool in place of its own AI writing feature.
data.authors: Researched and written by Content Cucumber. Featuring Mathew Adams (Adeia), George Lawton, Chris Sheridan, Matt Swan, Karen Sage and Lizzy Adams.

data.title: What the answers showed
data.subtitle: Four findings from the first edition.

items.title: A human owns the output.
items.text: Half the people who answered gave a third answer between yes and no. AI helps with research, drafts and editing, and a person owns what gets published. Karen Sage put it in one line. “To help create content yes, but not to create content by itself.”

items.title: People who write for a living said no the most.
items.text: Writers and copywriters together returned 41% no answers, against 14% across the whole study.

items.title: The people building AI disagree with each other.
items.text: AI practitioners spread across five positions. 11% of them said it is not a choice to make, against 2% across the study.

items.title: A name attached changes the answer.
items.text: In the LinkedIn poll, where no name is attached, 18% of votes said no, against 12% by message.

items.question: What is this study?
items.answer: One question, asked of people who work in commerce, content and AI. Should companies use AI to create content, and why? 363 answers came in, 246 by direct message, 27 in person at eTail Boston and 90 as LinkedIn poll votes.

items.question: Who is running it?
items.answer: Brent Peterson and Isaac Morey at Content Cucumber. There is no sponsor and no client behind the question.

items.question: How much does it cost?
items.answer: Nothing. Enter your details and we email you the full study as a PDF.

items.question: I answered the question. Am I in it?
items.answer: Your answer was read, coded and counted. The study quotes a selection of answers, and anonymous answers carry no name and no employer.

items.question: Will there be another edition?
items.answer: Yes. We will run it twice a year, track the trends and refer back to earlier reports.

items.question: Will I get sales emails?
items.answer: You will get the study and the occasional note from Content Cucumber. You can unsubscribe at any time, and we do not share your details.
